concept: Lavender drapery portrait in a parked scooter garage
creativeDirection: Editorial location photography in a real industrial garage corner, using a physically built scene and crisp naturalistic light to restage the strongest portrait within one plausible place.
scene: In a quiet indoor scooter garage or repair bay, a corner has been softened by hanging translucent lavender fabric and pale painted walls; a parked vintage scooter sits nearby, and one woman reclines on layered fabric on a low platform or padded mechanic's creeper while two large dogs press against her, turning the utilitarian space unexpectedly tender.

elements.element: the woman from reference image 1 reclining with the two large dogs on pooled sheer lavender fabric
a real vintage scooter parked close behind her, angled so its body and mirrors are clearly visible
a cream and red art deco garage door panel and circular speaker-like wall vents echoing the airship cover's architecture
a bold yellow-painted service bay stripe on the wall with rounded purple tool shadows radiating behind the subject
a stark white work cabinet with a horizontal blue band near its base
a red metal shop lamp with a jagged sun-like guard hanging above the scene

mood: dreamlike tenderness inside a practical workspace

prompt: A real indoor scooter garage corner photographed from a low eye-level angle, close and slightly off-centre, with shallow-to-moderate depth and the space wrapping tightly around the subject rather than opening into a deep passage. The primary subject is the woman from reference image 1, reclined on pooled sheer lavender fabric spread over a low padded platform in the garage, with the two large dogs from reference image 1 pressed closely against her; keep her recognisable to the reference image with the same reclining pose, dark hair spread around her head, calm expression, and direct dreamy stillness, all lit by the room's late afternoon window light. Behind and beside her, include the vintage scooter from reference image 3 as a real parked vehicle angled across the middle ground with its mirrors visible, integrated naturally into the bay. Add a cream-and-red art deco garage door panel and circular wall vents inspired by reference image 4, a bold yellow wall section with soft rounded purple radiating tool shadows inspired by reference image 2, a stark white work cabinet with a blue horizontal band near the bottom inspired by reference image 6, and a red metal shop lamp with a jagged sun-like protective guard inspired by reference image 7. Photoreal editorial location photography, crisp and clean, no haze, no collage look, no text anywhere. Keep the composition intimate and asymmetrical, faces fully readable, the scooter and supports secondary to the reclining figure and dogs. Use late afternoon window light mixed with soft interior fill so the lavender fabric, yellow wall, cream surfaces, and red details all read clearly at small size. Palette of lavender, cream, yellow, purple, red, and white; mood dreamlike, strange, and tender inside a practical industrial room. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 1 shows one woman reclining with two dogs, and reference image 9 is an enlarged close-up of those same people - take their faces from reference image 9. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, and do not get round that by copying a sleeve flat onto a mural, banner, poster, billboard, tapestry, wall panel, screen, monitor, television, sign, cut-out, or floor graphic, or carving it as a wall-mounted relief; show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, display, sign, or silhouette anywhere; transform their non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
